idiom_name: unittest.mock Mock/MagicMock with return_value and side_effect
implementation_notes: unittest.mock is the stdlib answer and states its purpose directly: the Mock class 'removes the need to create a host of stubs throughout your test suite'. A stub is Mock() with return_value set - or side_effect for an exception, a function, or an iterable of consecutive answers - injected by passing it to the SUT, or installed with patch()/patch.object replacing the attribute where the SUT looks it up. What replaces the hand-written stub class is the configurable mock object plus patch; the hand-written class (or a Protocol implementation) stays justified when the collaborator must be a genuine instance or when the answer depends on arguments. Use spec/spec_set or autospec so typos in method names fail instead of silently creating a child mock.
code_sketch:
from unittest.mock import Mock

warehouse = Mock()
warehouse.has_inventory.return_value = False

order = Order("Talisker", 50)
assert order.fill(warehouse) is False
pitfalls: A bare Mock answers every attribute and call, so a misspelled method creates a child mock and the test passes; pin the interface with spec, spec_set or autospec.
patch() must target the name where the SUT looks it up (the module under test), not the module that defines it.
An unconfigured Mock's default return value is another Mock, which is truthy and satisfies 'is not None'; configure every answer the branch under test consumes.

variants.name: Hand-written stub class or Protocol implementation
variants.idiom_name: small class (or Protocol implementation) with canned returns
variants.implementation_notes: Python's duck typing makes the classic form a two-line class: whatever has the called method and returns the canned value is a valid collaborator, so class StubWarehouse: def has_inventory(self, sku, qty): return False suffices, and no framework is needed. Annotating the SUT's parameter with a typing.Protocol documents the contract and lets a type checker notice a renamed or misspelled method that duck typing would hide; the class also composes naturally when the collaborator must be a real instance (a context manager, an iterable, an object with __slots__) where MagicMock's permissiveness gets in the way. Keep one stub per test or parametrize the class so it does not accumulate answers.
pitfalls: Duck typing hides signature drift: annotate the collaborator parameter as a Protocol so a type checker catches the rename that a Mock would also swallow.
A hand-written stub reused across tests accumulates state and stops being predictable; create it per test or reset its fields.
Special methods (__enter__, __iter__, __call__) are looked up on the type, so configuring them on an instance of a hand-written class does not work - implement them on the class.
